knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Proved that every closed knight's tour on any n*n board (n >= 5) has >= 4 oblique turns. The proof is purely algebraic, generalizing Knuth's 8x8 result. Key theorem: four_oblique_corners exhibits 4 distinct positions (the corners) where turns are oblique because the dot product of entry/exit vectors is always -4.
builtItems: Created KnightsTourObliqueOQ01.lean: parameterized board, knight graph, corner analysis, main theorem
Proved cornerXX_neighbors: degree-2 theorems for all 4 corners (algebraic elimination of 6/8 offsets)
Proved corner_forces_oblique: universal oblique turn theorem at any corner (dot = -4)
Proved four_oblique_corners: 4 distinct oblique positions exist in any closed tour on n*n (n >= 5)
Created gallery entry with meta.json, annotations.json, index.ts
insights: For n >= 5, each corner of the n*n board has exactly 2 knight-adjacent squares (6 of 8 offsets produce negative coordinates, impossible in Fin n)
The dot product of entry/exit move vectors at any corner is always -4, independent of board size: (-offset1) . offset2 = -(1*2 + 2*1) = -4
The corner-forcing mechanism is purely algebraic — no native_decide or enumeration needed, unlike the 8x8 parent proof
The bound 4 is tight: the 8x8 board achieves exactly 4 oblique turns via Knuth's unique minimum tour
nextSteps: Does the minimum oblique count grow with n? Investigate whether boards with n >> 8 have minimum > 4
Can edge squares (degree 3-4) also force oblique turns under certain conditions?
